title: Laughs! — Audible Contagion
subtitle: Situated laughter, acoustic contagion, recovery, and quiet aftermath
lineage: Lineage: Daniel Mercadante / The Mercadantes, Laughs!
theorem: Build a changing acoustic chain from individually situated laughter, allowing rhythm to spread between shots while retaining the difference between people laughing together and an editor making separate recordings answer one another.
boundary_note: No person becomes an unconsenting target through the adjacent image. Separate source contexts are established first before acoustic pulses overlap.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #04 (t=12.50s-17.70s): `bcd1491c` shows a wooden medical tongue depressor inside an open mouth during an oral exam.
Seg #06 (t=22.20s-27.70s): `e15366de` cuts internally at t=27.04s (clip 4.8s) from the laughing audience chorus to a stage magician.
Seg #07 (t=27.70s-34.20s): `2144d337` has a burned-in lower-third banner obscuring the recovery shot.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: Seg #04 mistakes an open mouth with a wooden medical tongue depressor for a 'situated solo laugh', breaking the contagious laughter chain.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: OpenCLIP visual false positive matching an open mouth to 'person laughing' without detecting the medical instrument, plus an unclamped tail cut at 4.8s in `e15366de`.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Replace Seg #04 with verified smiling/laughing conversation shot `bf3ca7be` (0.05s-3.20s); clamp `e15366de` to `0.2s-4.4s` before the cut at 4.79s; replace Seg #07 with verified unbannered recovery shot `f004b127` (4.5s-8.8s).
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: The opening contained laugh in Seg #02 (`655567b6`, `Back-Room Boy`, 1942), `bd6a3b8a`, `7deb911c`, and the quiet curtained room-tone aftermath in Seg #08 (`491529e4`).
